text:
Jordan (Support): FYI customer on Dedicated is seeing intermittent 429s + latency spikes despite being inside their reserved throughput. Root says: committed 120 qps, bursts ~250 qps for short windows, seeing 429s starting ~2026-03-10T14:02Z. They attached request/response headers.

Maya (Infra SRE): can you paste the headers and a minimal repro? curious if it's our gateway rate cap or per-pool enforcement.

Jordan (Support): pasted headers: 
```
x-request-id: c2f3aa7b
x-reserved-pool-id: rp-93a7
x-customer-plan: dedicated-monthly
x-commit-qps: 120
x-observed-qps: 238
x-rate-limit: 120/60
x-retry-after: 6
status: 429
error: rate_limit_exceeded
```
Plus auth header looked fine (Bearer token). Customer says their load pattern is many short spikes (~1-2s) of 240-300 qps every 30s.

Akshay (Platform): quick notes: Dedicated has two separate caps applied in series: the committed QPS (per-pool steady limit) and a short-term smoothing/burst window. If spike >> smoothing_window, gateway will trim down to commit and return 429s if tokens exhausted. We also have a controller that enforces per-route concurrency slots which can show as latency if saturated.

Jess (Customer Ops): customer insists their SLA doc says "allow short bursts up to 250 qps for up to 3s". They have logs showing average under commit but bursts exceed.

Maya (Infra SRE): ok repro steps I want to run: 1) show recent pool enforcement events: `rlog query "pool_event where pool_id=\"rp-93a7\" | sort ts desc | limit 50` 2) check gateway bucket tokens: `infractl pool tokens rp-93a7 --window 60 --detail` 3) trace a 429 trace id (if they provided x-request-id) with `trace fetch c2f3aa7b`

Jordan (Support): ran step 1 + 2 with customer permission, logs attached. Seeing repeated `token_exhausted` events at 14:02:11, 14:02:41, 14:03:13 etc. Token bucket shows burst capacity 60 tokens for the pool, smoothing window 30s.

Maya (Infra SRE): aha - burst capacity 60 tokens means short bursts above commit saturate quickly. If customer expects 250 qps bursts from commit 120, they'd need burst tokens >= (250-120)*burst_duration ≈ 130 tokens for a 1s burst. Current settings are too small.

Akshay (Platform): that config is controlled by the pool profile: `burst_size`, `smoothing_window`, and `overcommit_policy`. For Dedicated we default burst_size conservatively to avoid noisy neighbors. We have an `allow_customer_burst` flag that can be toggled per-customer when purchased as an add-on.

Jordan (Support): customer says they never bought an add-on. They thought their SLA encompassed those bursts. Could be a docs mismatch. Also they reported some 401s few mins earlier — possible token refresh thrash — but most failures are 429s.

Jess (Customer Ops): I'll check the contract. Meanwhile we should propose a workaround to avoid customer service disruption.

Maya (Infra SRE): immediate mitigation options: 
- Increase burst_size for rp-93a7 to 140 temporarily (use `infractl pool update rp-93a7 --burst-size 140`) and monitor.
- Enable per-route queueing smoothing (adds <50ms avg latency) by flipping `smoothing_queue` -> `true` for the route.
- Advise customer to shift to a small client-side token-bucket library to smooth spikes (we can provide code snippet).

Akshay (Platform): addition: ensure per-route rate settings are not lower than pool commit (route-level rate caps can produce unexpected 429 even if pool has capacity). Check route config: `platformctl route show cust-abc/model-endpoint`

Jordan (Support): did route check: route had `max_rate: 120` and `burst_override: null`. So route is aligned but no burst override.

Maya (Infra SRE): two big takeaways: 1) Gateway enforces several tiers (route, pool, global). 2) Bursting across short windows consumes burst tokens; once exhausted we 429.

Jordan (Support): customer also attached a trace where request headers show `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `x-forwarded-for` with many IPs, they use a load balancer that does short-lived connections. Could LB behavior exacerbate token drain?

Maya (Infra SRE): yes — concurrent connections multiplied by client-side retry/backoff can simulate large instantaneous qps. Ask them to sample incoming concurrency and retries.

Jess (Customer Ops): contract review: SLA says "best-effort short bursts up to 200 qps" — so mismatch with customer expectation of 250. We'll propose either a small temporary config change or upgrade add-on.

Billing (FinOps): flag: if we increase burst_size as a one-off, inform finance — this could increase billable usage. Also if auth thrash exists (401 loops), that can create extra failed requests billed differently. We should check invoicing for the day.

Jordan (Support): proposed immediate action plan (short-term): 
1) Offer to enable `smoothing_queue` on their route for 24h as low-risk (no customer code change).
2) If they accept, schedule a brief config change: `platformctl route update cust-abc/model-endpoint --smoothing-queue true` (need Maya to approve).
3) If smoothing insufficient, offer temporary burst_size bump to 140 for 2 hours while customer implements client-side smoothing or purchases burst add-on.
4) Ask customer to share a lightweight stress script we can run in staging to reproduce.

Maya (Infra SRE): I can do step 2 and 3. Before bumping, will run a quick impact sim on pooled nodes: `infractl simulate-burst --pool rp-93a7 --qps 260 --duration 3s` — that should show if noisy neighbor risk is acceptable.

Akshay (Platform): I will also check whether pool has other tenants with similar allocations. We should avoid changing burst_size if it could cause sustained resource pressure. If the sim passes and no other critical tenants, proceed.

Jordan (Support): customer asks for a reproducible script. Suggested one-liner (bash + curl) to generate a short spike: 
```
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' &
done; wait
```
They agreed to run it in staging.

Maya (Infra SRE): after sim: results: 3s 260qps spike triggered burst token exhaustion, gateway returned 429s after ~1.6s. No other pools impacted in sim. I'll proceed with a temporary bump to 140 for 2h and enable smoothing_queue.

SRE-Bot: Deploy event recorded: `cfg-change rp-93a7 burst_size=140 smoothing_queue=true by maya at 2087654542`

Jordan (Support): notified customer and asked them to re-run their spike test. They re-ran at 14:07Z and reported success: almost no 429s, a few 503-ish latency tails but acceptable. They will implement client-side smoothing next week.

Jess (Customer Ops): contract note: recommend we follow up to offer formal burst add-on with pricing. Also update docs to clarify SLA burst ceilings.

Billing (FinOps): confirmed: temporary bump will be tracked; we will not retro-bill but will note for recurring add-on discussion.

Maya (Infra SRE): action items: revert config after 2h if customer doesn't purchase add-on + check pool token refill metrics + add a small alert rule for `pool_burst_exhausted` to notify support earlier.

Akshay (Platform): platform action: add lint check that route-level `max_rate` and pool commit are surfaced in console UI with clear burst expectations.

Jordan (Support): final note to thread: customer now stable; moving to handshake with Customer Ops to propose add-on. Leaving this thread open for the revert and follow-up. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Maya (Infra SRE): marking as resolved for infra. I'll post revert event when it happens.

SRE-Bot: Config revert scheduled at 2087658342 (2h window) for rp-93a7 unless canceled.

Jordan (Support): closing loop when revert done and follow-up email sent.
